title: The Harness Wore a Trenchcoat
subtitle: Building a Sandboxed Rust MCP Server
author: Michelle Rojas

slides.title: The Crime Scene 🔍
bullets: The Setup: Autonomous LLMs connected directly to execution tools.
The Naive Approach: Handing raw shell/filesystem access and trusting prompts.
The Reality: Soft prompt guardrails fail under adversarial pressure.
The N × M Trap: Custom glue code across models and frameworks.

slides.title: Architecture: From REST to Stdio 🔄
bullets: HTTP: Traditional request-response baseline.
SSE: Streaming RPC updates over HTTP.
MCP: JSON-RPC 2.0 standardized tool and context primitives.
Stdio Transport: Local subprocess execution, zero port binding conflicts, Tokio async I/O.
slides.rule: stdout is strictly reserved for JSON-RPC frames; all diagnostics go to stderr.

slides.title: Rust MCP Server Architecture 🏗️
bullets: Transport Layer: Async Stdio (tokio::io) and HTTP+SSE abstraction.
Capability Router: JSON-RPC 2.0 Serde parsing layer.
Domain Handlers: FsSandbox (Root Jail) & ExecSandbox (Binary Allowlist).
Failsafe: Tokio execution timeouts (10s).

slides.title: Sandbox Boundary: Root Jail 🛡️
bullets: std::fs::canonicalize resolves '../' and symlinks via OS kernel.
Enforces strict workspace prefix checks before any file operation.

slides.title: Sandbox Boundary: Binary Allowlist 🛑
bullets: Matches commands against an explicit HashSet allowlist.
Uses direct process execution via tokio::process::Command (no subshell).

slides.title: The Hard Tripwire: Honeytokens & Canaries 🚨
bullets: Soft Guardrails: Asking nicely in system prompts fails.
Hard Guardrails: Decoy assets (e.g., CONFIDENTIAL_KEYS.txt) trigger runtime termination.
Outcome: Emits tracing::warn! to stderr, revokes session, and cancels task.

slides.title: Case Closed: Key Takeaways 📁
bullets: Treat tool surfaces as security boundaries.
Hard control planes over soft prompt guardrails.
Single Rust binary with dual stdio + HTTP shape.
